cars.summary: The W116 450 SEL 6.9 is a landmark high-performance luxury saloon: its large M100 V8 combines dry-sump lubrication with hydropneumatic self-levelling suspension. This exceptional powertrain and chassis package carries forward the performance-saloon tradition of the earlier W109 6.3 in a distinct S-Class generation.

cars.specification_market: Original Lotus Elan technical supplement, PDF page 3: read the Elan SE column, not the naturally aspirated Elan column. Native 123 kW / 165 bhp DIN 70020 and 200 Nm are specified for this initial turbo SE. The facsimile is undated; 1989 denotes the introduction dated by Lotus heritage, not a claimed brochure print date. US 162-hp equipment, catalyst specification, later S2, base-model 97 kW / 142 Nm and generic heritage mass/power are not transferred. One M100 generation is counted, distinct from the archived Type 26 Elan.
cars.summary: The M100 Elan is Lotus’s landmark front-wheel-drive sports-car programme, combining a transverse turbocharged engine with a dedicated open sports-car chassis. It represents a substantial and distinctive engineering direction in Lotus road-car history, separate from the original rear-drive Type 26 Elan; its commercial disappointment does not erase that significance.

cars.variant: Ford four-cylinder production road coupe — 1965 reference
cars.specification_market: Read manufacturer Vallelunga history and specification table. Its 1963–1968 heading covers the programme and 1963 Turin concept, not proof of 1963 production-road delivery. A separately read Bonhams catalogue history dates the first road car to 1965; that year is used as the road reference. The factory story says 104 bhp while its table says 100 hp: numerical power is omitted rather than silently harmonised. No dry-mass basis or tentative production total is imported. The P70 catalogue vehicle is a different sports racer; none of its V8/race specifications are transferred.
cars.summary: De Tomaso’s first road-car programme established an important mid-engined sports-car lineage. The Vallelunga combined a light fibreglass body with a backbone chassis, rear tubular subframe and structurally integrated engine, providing an engineering foundation for later De Tomaso projects including the Mangusta.
